findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() applies math.floor()/math.ceil() directly to getattr(item, self.key). Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders by -datetime, so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor() calls this key function for non-empty result sets, so the first non-empty optimized audit-log page returns a 500 instead of results. It should reuse DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion rather than the numeric Paginator implementation.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator does not convert cursor timestamps to datetimes
findings.body: value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. For audit logs that value is the millisecond epoch timestamp produced by DateTimePaginator-style cursors, but BasePaginator.build_queryset() compares it directly against the datetime column. Unlike DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor(), which converts the timestamp to an aware datetime, this passes a number into a datetime comparison, causing a database/type error or incorrect filtering on every page after the first.

findings.title: Negative offsets do not work on Django querysets
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, this code executes queryset[negative_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly reject negative slicing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'); they do not automatically handle it as the comments claim. A crafted cursor such as '0:-5:0' therefore produces an unhandled 500 rather than the claimed efficient reverse pagination. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError or normalized before slicing.

findings.title: BasePaginator still allows negative offsets for previous-page cursors
findings.body: The new boundary handling clamps negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false: 'max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset'. A user-supplied cursor with is_prev=1 and a negative offset, for example '<value>:-5:1', still reaches queryset[negative:stop] and raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. This affects all existing BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoints, not just the optimized audit-log path; negative offsets should be consistently rejected or clamped before slicing.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: This line unconditionally dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access for every non-superuser request, and it is evaluated even when optimized_pagination is not requested. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional and can be None for principals granted organization access without an organization membership. For such requests this newly added code raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working default pagination path; it needs a None check or an access-based check.

findings.title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, negative-offset behavior, and a query-parameter/superuser gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. Tests using the audit-log endpoint's actual -datetime ordering, multi-page cursors, previous-page cursors, and negative offsets would have caught the datetime-key crash, timestamp-conversion bug, and Django negative-slicing failure before merge.
